THESE APPEALS COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 COMMON JUDGMENT
These appeals are filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('MV Act' for short).

MFA No.6880/2012 is filed by the Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award passed in MVC No.4321/2010, while MFA No.6881/2012 is filed by Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award  -6-  NC: 2023:KHC:41429  MFA No. 6880 of 2012  C/W MFA No. 6049 of 2012
MFA No. 6881 of 2012 passed in MVC No.4345/2010 and MFA No.6049/2012 is filed by the claimant in MVC No.4321/2010.

Since all these appeals are arising out of common judgment in MVC No.4321/2010 & MVC No.4345/2010 and arising out of the same accident, they are heard together and disposed of through this common judgment.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties herein are referred as per the ranks occupied by them before the Tribunal.

3. The brief factual matrix leading to the case are as under:
The Divisional Manager vs K Venugopal on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42072374/
5  On 21.02.2005, at about 7.15 p.m., the petitioners were traveling from Thirupathi towards Bangalore in Maruthi Van bearing registration No.KA-19-M-0268.

When they reached near Ontillu, the driver of tractor bearing No.ATN-9558 came suddenly on the road from left in a rash and negligent manner and in a reverse direction and at the same time, another tractor bearing registration No.KA-P-04-U-3199 tried to cross the road from its left  -7-  NC: 2023:KHC:41429  MFA No. 6880 of 2012  C/W MFA No. 6049 of 2012  MFA No. 6881 of 2012 side to right side and as a result, they collided with each other.
As a result, both these tractors together dashed against the Maruti Van in which the petitioners were travelling.
The petitioner in MVC No.4345/2010 was driving the Maruti Van.
As a result of the accident, one of the inmate of the Maruti Van succumbed and petitioners suffered grievous injuries.
They were initially taken treatment in Local hospital at Chittor and later on, they were shifted to C.M.C. Hospital, Vellore and then referred to Mallya Hospital, Bangalore.
They under went surgery during the course of their hospitalization.

Subsequently,
the case was registered against the petitioner in MVC No.4345/2010 and he appeared before the concerned police and obtained bail and later on he was acquitted in CC.No.415/2005.

The petitioners claim that they were hale and healthy and due to accidental injuries, they suffered The Divisional Manager vs K Venugopal on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42072374/
6
both physically and mentally and hence, they filed claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- and Rs.5,00,000/- with interest respectively, as against respondent Nos.1, 2 & 4.

It is asserted that the accident is  -8-  NC: 2023:KHC:41429  MFA No. 6880 of 2012  C/W MFA No. 6049 of 2012  MFA No. 6881 of 2012 because of actionable negligence on the part of the drivers of both the tractors and hence, both these petitioners have filed claim petitions under Section 166 of the MV Act.
Respondent Nos.1 & 2 are the owners of the two tractors which were involved in the accident, while respondent No.3 is the insurer of the Maruti Van which was involved in the accident.

4. Respondent No.3 resisted the claim petition on various grounds and further asserted that the Maruti Van was belonging to claimant in MVC No.4321/2010 and it was driven by her husband, who is the claimant in MVC No.4345/2010.

It is asserted that MVC No.4865/2005 is already filed against the present claimants by the legal representatives of the deceased, who was the inmate of the Maruti Van and claim petition came to be allowed by dismissing the claim as against respondent No.3/
appellant/Insurance Company, but the liability was fastened on claimants and the said petition was contested by the claimants.

It is also asserted that, there is a finding The Divisional Manager vs K Venugopal on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42072374/
7  -9-  NC: 2023:KHC:41429  MFA No. 6880 of 2012  C/W MFA No. 6049 of 2012  MFA No. 6881 of 2012 that the accident is because of actionable negligence on the part of the driver i.e., claimant in MFA No.4345/2010 and since there is no additional premium paid covering the liability of inmates of the car, the question of fastening the liability on Insurance Company does not arise at all.
Hence, the Insurance Company has sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
 5.

After appreciating the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal has held that the accident in question is because of actionable negligence on the part of drivers of both the tractors and liability was fastened on respondent No.3/Insurance Company to pay the compensation.
In MVC No.4321/2010 compensation of Rs.1,42,000/- came to be awarded, while in MVC No.4345/2010 compensation of Rs.65,000/- came to be awarded.

Being aggrieved by this judgment and award,
the claimant in MVC No.4321/2010, who is the owner of the Maruti Van filed MFA No.6049/2012 seeking the  - 10 -  NC: 2023:KHC:41429  MFA No. 6880 of 2012  C/W MFA No. 6049 of 2012  MFA No. 6881 of 2012 enhancement, while the Insurance Company has filed the other two MFAs challenging the liability.

The Divisional Manager vs K Venugopal on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42072374/
8  6. Heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company and learned counsel for the respondents/claimants.
Perused the records.

7. The learned counsel for appellant would contend that the claimants were inmates of Maruti Van and the claimant in MVC No.4321/2010 claims to have lost one eye sight, but to prove the disability, the Doctor was not examined.
It is asserted that when the policy simply discloses the liability covered pertaining to owner cum driver and no premium was paid covering the risk of the other inmates.

It is also submitted that a claim petition was filed by legal representatives of the deceased in respect of the said accident itself in MVC No.4865/2005,
wherein the liability is fastened on the present claimants and claim petition against the Insurance Company was rejected which was challenged by the claimants in  - 11 -  NC: 2023:KHC:41429  MFA No. 6880 of 2012  C/W MFA No. 6049 of 2012  MFA No. 6881 of 2012 MFA No.8561/2009, but the same was withdrawn unconditionally.
Hence, he would contend that now they cannot maintain the petition claiming compensation.

He would also assert that the accident has occurred on 21.02.2005 and the claim petitions were filed on The Divisional Manager vs K Venugopal on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42072374/
9 09.07.2010.

But prior to the same, the claim petitions by other claimants were filed wherein the present claimants were respondent Nos.1 & 2 and they have contested the matter and they were disposed of against them.

Hence, he would contend that the claim petitions are clearly barred by law of limitations considering the date of cause of action under Article 137 of Limitation Act, 1963, as the period of limitation is 3 years for filing claim petition.
He would contend that the petition is filed after 5 years and the premium was paid covering the risk of owner cum driver.

But owner was not driving and her husband was driving and hence, claim petitions are not maintainable that too when liability is already fastened on them and they have admitted the same by withdrawing the MFA.
Hence, he would seek for allowing the appeals.
C/W MFA No. 6049 of 2012  MFA No. 6881 of 2012

8. Per contra, the learned counsel for respondents/appellants in MFA No.6049/2012 would contend that the claimant-owner was a passenger and suffered sight of right eye and it is admittedly a permanent disability.

Though the Doctor is not examined,
the evidence regarding disability is undisputed and no proper income was taken and compensation awarded under pain and suffering and loss of amenities was on lower side and no compensation was awarded under loss The Divisional Manager vs K Venugopal on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42072374/
10 of future income including conveyance, food and nourishment.
It is further submitted that premium was paid pertaining to owner cum driver and claimant being the owner is entitled to receive the compensation under the contract.

Hence, he would seek for dismissal of the appeals filed by the Insurance Company and allow his appeal in MFA No.6049/2012.
 9.

Having heard the arguments and perusing the records, it is evident that the Maruti Van bearing registration No.KA-19-M-0268 was involved in the accident  - 13 -  NC: 2023:KHC:41429  MFA No. 6880 of 2012  C/W MFA No. 6049 of 2012  MFA No. 6881 of 2012 dated 21.02.2005.
It is also an undisputed fact that both the claimants suffered injuries and one Bhanumathi who was an inmate of the Maritu Van succumbed in the said accident because of accidental injuries.
It is also the undisputed fact that the Maruti Van was insured with respondent No.3 i.e., the appellant in MFA No.6880/2012 & MFA No.6881/2012.
It is also an undisputed fact that Maruti Van was driven by K.Venugopal, the husband of the owner who is the claimant in MVC No.4345/2010.
All these aspects are undisputed.

10. It is also an undisputed fact that the legal representatives of the Bhanumathi have filed a claim The Divisional Manager vs K Venugopal on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42072374/
11 petition in MVC No.4865/2005 before MACT (SCCH-10),
Bangalore.

In the said case, the present claimants i.e.,
Arunakumari and K.Venugopal were arrayed as respondent Nos.1 & 2 and they appeared and contested the matter,
while appellant/Insurance Company in the other two appeals was respondent No.3 in the said case.

The claimants herein who were respondent Nos.1 & 2 in the  - 14 -  NC: 2023:KHC:41429  MFA No. 6880 of 2012  C/W MFA No. 6049 of 2012  MFA No. 6881 of 2012 said claim petition, contested the matter and the claimant K.Venugopal was also examined as RW1.

After appreciating the oral and documentary evidence, the said claim petition came to be allowed in part as against Arunakumari, who was the owner of the Maruti Van and claim against others including the Insurance Company,
came to be dismissed.

11 . It is also evident from the records that the owner-Arunakumari claimant in MVC No.4321/2010 who is appellant in MFA No.6049/2012 has challenged this award passed against her in MVC No.4865/2005 in MFA No.8561/2009.
However, subsequently, the said MFA was withdrawn unconditionally vide order dated 11.09.2014.
In view of the withdrawal of MFA No.8561/2009, the claimant/Arunakumari has admitted her liability.

Hence,
question will arise as to whether she can maintain a The Divisional Manager vs K Venugopal on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42072374/
12 petition against herself and as to whether any additional premium was paid covering the risk of the inmates.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: MFA No. 6881 of 2012
12. Admittedly, the vehicle was driven by K.Venugopal who is the husband of owner-Arunakumari.
The policy is marked at Ex.R4 and relevant portion is marked on EX.R4(a) which disclose that additional premium of Rs.100/- is paid covering the risk of the owner cum driver.
Admittedly, Arunakumari was not driving the vehicle and her husband was driving the vehicle.
Much arguments have been advanced by the learned counsel appearing for Insurance Company that the liability is covered only if Arunakumari-owner was driving the offending vehicle.
But the said arguments holds no water in view of the decision reported in AIR 2009 SC 3056 [Ningamma vs. United India Insurance Company].

entities.text: AIR 2009 SC 3056 [Ningamma vs. United India Insurance Company]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court in the said decision clearly held that the driver being husband of the owner, steps into shoes of the owner.
Exactly the same situation is prevailing in the instant case as K.Venugopal being the husband of the owner-Arunakumari was driving the vehicle and steps into the shoes of the owner.
In view of this, as per Ex.P4, the risk of only K.Venugopal is covered.

C/W MFA No. 6049 of 2012 The Divisional Manager vs K Venugopal on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42072374/
13  MFA No. 6881 of 2012
Admittedly, though the owner was travelling in the vehicle as a passenger but from Ex.R4 it is evident that no separate additional premium was paid covering the risk of the inmates.
Under such circumstances, the question of Insurance Company paying any compensation to Arunakumari does not arise at all.

The liability of Insurance Company would be as against her husband K.Venugopal who was driving the vehicle who steps into the shoes of the owner in view of the Nigamma's decision referred supra.
 13.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.65,000/- to K.Venugopal and he has not challenged that award seeking any enhancement.
It is only Arunakumari who is seeking enhancement and as observed above, her risk is not covered.
As such, the appeal filed by Arunakumari in MFA No.6049/2012 is not at all maintainable and needs to be dismissed straight away.
Under Policy premium of Rs.100 was paid covering the risk of owner cum driver and risk was to the extent of Rs.2,00,000/-.

Hence, the Insurance Company i.e., respondent No.3 is liable to indemnify to the extent of The Divisional Manager vs K Venugopal on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42072374/
14 Rs.2,00,000/- out of contractual liability.
 15.

entities.text: Divisional Manager vs K Venugopal on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The other contentions raised by the appellant Insurance Company is regarding limitation.

Admittedly,
the accident has occurred on 21.02.2005 and claim petitions were filed on 09.07.2010.
The learned counsel for appellant/Insurance Company has invited the attention of the Court to Article 137 of the Limitation Act.

Admittedly,
under the MV Act no provision is made prescribing limitation for filing the claim petition.
Apart from that, this defence was not at all set up before the Tribunal, though objection statement was filed elaborately.
Though it is argued that no issue was framed in this regard, when the specific defence itself is not raised before the Tribunal, the question of framing the issue on limitation does not arise at all.
Further, under the MV Act no limitation was  - 18 -  NC: 2023:KHC:41429  MFA No. 6880 of 2012  C/W MFA No. 6049 of 2012  MFA No. 6881 of 2012 prescribed for filing claim petition.

Article 137 was relied by the learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company but, it is pertaining to any other application for which no period of limitation is provided elsewhere and the limitation prescribed is three years from right to apply accrues.
This Article 137 is not pertaining to original proceedings, but it is pertaining to other applications to be filed.

Initially there was a specific provision prescribing the The Divisional Manager vs K Venugopal on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42072374/
15 limitation, but subsequently, by way of amendment the said provision was removed.

In view of the same,
considering that Article 137 is not applicable to the petitions and it is applicable to applications only, the arguments regarding limitation cannot be entertained.

16. In view of these facts & circumstances, MFA No.6881/2012 filed by the Insurance Company and MFA No.6049/2012 filed by the owner-Arunakumari are not at all maintainable as the Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation under contract upto Rs.2,00,000/- in view of premium having been received to the extent of Rs.100/-
 - 19 -  NC: 2023:KHC:41429  MFA No. 6880 of 2012  C/W MFA No. 6049 of 2012  MFA No. 6881 of 2012 But in MVC No.4345/2010 only compensation of Rs.65,000/- was awarded and the K.Venugopal, who was claimant in MVC No.4345/2010 has not sought any enhancement.
Hence, Insurance Company is liable to pay the said compensation.

However, MFA No.6880/2012 arising out of MVC No.4321/2010 needs to be allowed as owner claimant/Arunakumari has not paid any additional premium and since her husband was driving the vehicle,
she is only an inmate and not covered under the policy.

17 . Looking to these facts & circumstances, MFA No.6880/2012 only needs to be allowed, while other two The Divisional Manager vs K Venugopal on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42072374/
16 appeals needs to be dismissed.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER (i) MFA No.6880/2012 filed by the insurance company/respondent No.3 is allowed.
The impugned judgment and award passed in MVC No.4321/2010 by the MACT is set aside and claim petition stands dismissed.
- 20 - NC: 2023:KHC:41429 (ii) MFA No.6881/2012 and MFA No.6049/2012 stand dismissed.
(iii) The statutory deposit made in MFA No.6880/2012 pertaining to MVC No.4321/2010 shall be returned to the Insurance Company.
(iv) The statutory deposit made by the Insurance Company in the appeal i.e., MFA No.6881/2012 shall be transmitted to the Tribunal for disbursement.

opennyai_summary.facts:
These appeals are filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('MV Act' for short).
The petitioner in MVC No.4345/2010 was driving the Maruti Van.
After appreciating the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal has held that the accident in question is because of actionable negligence on the part of drivers of both the tractors and liability was fastened on respondent No.3/Insurance Company to pay the compensation.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Admittedly, Arunakumari was not driving the vehicle and her husband was driving the vehicle.
But the said arguments holds no water in view of the decision reported in AIR 2009 SC 3056 [Ningamma vs. United India Insurance Company].
The Hon'ble Apex Court in the said decision clearly held that the driver being husband of the owner, steps into shoes of the owner.
Exactly the same situation is prevailing in the instant case as K.Venugopal being the husband of the owner-Arunakumari was driving the vehicle and steps into the shoes of the owner.
In view of this, as per Ex.P4, the risk of only K.Venugopal is covered.
Admittedly, though the owner was travelling in the vehicle as a passenger but from Ex.R4 it is evident that no separate additional premium was paid covering the risk of the inmates.
Under such circumstances, the question of Insurance Company paying any compensation to Arunakumari does not arise at all.
The liability of Insurance Company would be as against her husband K.Venugopal who was driving the vehicle who steps into the shoes of the owner in view of the Nigamma's decision referred supra.
 13.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.65,000/- to K.Venugopal and he has not challenged that award seeking any enhancement.
It is only Arunakumari who is seeking enhancement and as observed above, her risk is not covered.
Under Policy premium of Rs.100 was paid covering the risk of owner cum driver and risk was to the extent of Rs.2,00,000/-.
